text.p: Following are the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Tuesday.
- Bosnian Federation president Kresimir Zubak pleased with the numbers of Croats who went to the polls.
- A record number of exhibitors to take part in the work of the Zagreb Autumn Trade Fair.
- Rumours of Prime Minister Zlatko Matesa being replaced are unfounded.
- The oil company INA has returned its prices to what they were before September 10, following an order by the Croatian government.
- 86 percent of former state-owned flats have now been sold to private owners.
- Minimal monthly cost of life in September: The prices of food up, prices of clothing down. Average family now needs 4,342 kuna per month.
- President Tudjman announces an annual economic growth of 7 percent. -- Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
